source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substring including written/read and other annotations.
source.public_versification_note: Exact XML records mapped to public labels; Zechariah 1:18–2:13 and Malachi 4 have different Hebrew chapter boundaries.

delta_method: F0 retained; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential choices flagged by the selective apparatus. Classification remains provisional. Overlap is triage only, with no change quota.

comparative_references.scope: Programmatic alignment after recovery of unfinished original-language drafts; selected bilingual rereads recorded separately. TSW is not the base text.

verses.rationale: Keeps the name while noting its literal my-messenger sense.
verses.before: The oracle of the word of the LORD to Israel by Malachi.
verses.after: An oracle: the word of the LORD to Israel through Malachi.
verses.tsw_comparator: The oracle of the word of the LORD to Israel by Malachi.

verses.rationale: Preserves the disputation and leads love into its contrasting next verse.
verses.before: “I have loved you,” says the LORD. But you say, “How have you loved us?” “Was not Esau Jacob's brother?” declares the LORD. “Yet I loved Jacob,
verses.after: “I have loved you,” says the LORD. But you ask, “How have you loved us?” “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother?” declares the LORD. “Yet I loved Jacob,
verses.tsw_comparator: “I have loved you,” says the LORD. But you say, “How have you loved us?” “Was not Esau Jacob's brother?” declares the LORD. “Yet I loved Jacob,

verses.rationale: Retains hated rather than silently weakening it and keeps the territorial devastation.
verses.before: but Esau I hated. I laid waste his hill country and gave his inheritance to the jackals of the wilderness.”
verses.after: but Esau I hated. I made his mountains a wasteland and his inheritance a place for desert jackals.”
verses.tsw_comparator: but Esau I hated. I laid waste his hill country and gave his inheritance to the jackals of the wilderness.”

verses.rationale: Keeps Edom’s resolve, divine response, and both judgment names.
verses.before: If Edom says, “We are shattered, but we will rebuild the ruins,” the LORD of Hosts says: “They may build, but I will tear down, and they will be called ‘The Wicked Land’ and ‘The People Against Whom the LORD Is Indignant Forever.’
verses.after: Edom may say, “We are shattered, but we will return and rebuild the ruins.” Yet the LORD of Armies says, “They may build, but I will tear down. They will be called ‘Wicked Territory’ and ‘The People with Whom the LORD Is Angry Forever.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: If Edom says, “We are shattered, but we will rebuild the ruins,” the LORD of Hosts says: “They may build, but I will tear down, and they will be called ‘The Wicked Land’ and ‘The People Against Whom the LORD Is Indignant Forever.’

verses.rationale: Preserves eyewitness recognition and beyond-Israel scope.
verses.before: Your eyes will see this, and you will say, ‘Great is the LORD beyond the borders of Israel.’”
verses.after: You will see it with your own eyes and say, “Great is the LORD beyond Israel’s borders!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Your eyes shall see this, and you shall say, ‘Great is the LORD beyond the borders of Israel.’”

verses.rationale: Retains the father/master questions, slavery relation, and named priestly addressees.
verses.before: “A son honors his father, and a servant his master. If then I am a father, where is my honor? And if I am a master, where is my fear?” says the LORD of Hosts to you, O priests who despise my name. But you say, ‘How have we despised your name?’
verses.after: “A son honors his father, and a slave his master. If I am a father, where is my honor? If I am a master, where is the fear of me?” says the LORD of Armies to you priests who despise my name. “But you ask, ‘How have we despised your name?’
verses.tsw_comparator: “A son honors his father, and a servant his master. If then I am a father, where is my honor? And if I am a master, where is my fear?” says the LORD of Hosts to you, O priests who despise my name. But you say, ‘How have we despised your name?’

verses.rationale: Keeps the you-object of pollution and the table/altar relation.
verses.before: “By offering polluted food upon my altar. But you say, ‘How have we polluted you?’ By saying that the table of the LORD may be despised.
verses.after: By presenting polluted food on my altar. You ask, ‘How have we polluted you?’ By saying, ‘The LORD’s table deserves contempt.’
verses.tsw_comparator: “By offering polluted food upon my altar. But you say, ‘How have we polluted you?’ By saying that the table of the LORD may be despised.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated accusation and pointed governor comparison.
verses.before: When you offer blind animals in sacrifice, is that not evil? And when you offer those that are lame or sick, is that not evil? Present that to your governor. Will he accept you or show you favor?” says the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: When you present blind animals for sacrifice, is that not wrong? When you present lame or sick animals, is that not wrong? Offer one to your governor! Would he be pleased with you or receive you favorably?” says the LORD of Armies.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you offer blind animals in sacrifice, is that not evil? And when you offer those that are lame or sick, is that not evil? Present that to your governor. Will he accept you or show you favor?” says the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Retains the us shift and the challenge tied to their offerings.
verses.before: “And now entreat the favor of God, that he may be gracious to us. With such a gift from your hand, will he show favor to any of you?” says the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: “Now seek God’s favor, so he may be gracious to us. With this coming from your hands, will he receive any of you favorably?” says the LORD of Armies.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And now entreat the favor of God, that he may be gracious to us. With such a gift from your hand, will he show favor to any of you?” says the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Keeps the wish to stop futile worship and explicit rejection.
verses.before: “Oh that there were one among you who would shut the doors, so that you might not kindle fire on my altar in vain. I have no pleasure in you,” says the LORD of Hosts, “and I will not accept an offering from your hand.
verses.after: “If only someone among you would shut the doors, so you would not kindle my altar for nothing! I take no pleasure in you,” says the LORD of Armies, “and I will accept no offering from your hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Oh that there were one among you who would shut the doors, so that you might not kindle fire on my altar in vain. I have no pleasure in you,” says the LORD of Hosts, “and I will not accept an offering from your hand.

verses.rationale: Preserves the present-form claim, repeated greatness, and worldwide offerings without imposing a future-only setting.
verses.before: For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name is great among the nations. In every place incense is offered to my name, and a pure offering. For my name is great among the nations,” says the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: For from sunrise to sunset my name is great among the nations. In every place incense and a pure offering are presented to my name, for my name is great among the nations,” says the LORD of Armies.
verses.tsw_comparator: For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name is great among the nations. In every place incense is offered to my name, and a pure offering. For my name is great among the nations,” says the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Preserves Lord rather than LORD here and the table-food insult.
verses.before: “But you profane it when you say, ‘The table of the LORD is polluted, and its fruit, that is, its food, may be despised.’
verses.after: “But you profane it by saying, ‘The Lord’s table is polluted, and its food is contemptible.’
verses.tsw_comparator: “But you profane it when you say, ‘The table of the LORD is polluted, and its fruit, that is, its food, may be despised.’

verses.rationale: Keeps disgust, stolen animals, and both divine-name formulas.
verses.before: You also say, ‘What a weariness this is,’ and you snort at it,” says the LORD of Hosts. “You bring what has been taken by violence, or is lame, or sick, and this you bring as your offering. Will I accept that from your hand?” says the LORD.
verses.after: You say, ‘What a burden!’ and sniff at it,” says the LORD of Armies. “You bring stolen, lame, and sick animals as your offering. Should I accept that from your hands?” says the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: You also say, ‘What a weariness this is,’ and you snort at it,” says the LORD of Hosts. “You bring what has been taken by violence, or is lame, or sick, and this you bring as your offering. Shall I accept that from your hand?” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the available male animal, deceitful substitution, and king title.
verses.before: “Cursed be the deceiver who has a male in his flock and vows it, yet sacrifices to the Lord what is blemished. For I am a great King,” says the LORD of Hosts, “and my name is feared among the nations.”
verses.after: “Cursed is the cheat who has a male in his flock and makes a vow but sacrifices a blemished animal to the Lord. For I am a great King,” says the LORD of Armies, “and my name is feared among the nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Cursed be the deceiver who has a male in his flock and vows it, yet sacrifices to the Lord what is blemished. For I am a great King,” says the LORD of Hosts, “and my name is feared among the nations.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the specific priestly address.
verses.before: “And now, O priests, this command is for you.
verses.after: Now, priests, this command is for you.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And now, O priests, this command is for you.

verses.rationale: Preserves both conditions, repeated taking-to-heart, and the already-accomplished curse.
verses.before: If you will not listen, and if you will not set it upon your heart to give honor to my name,” says the LORD of Hosts, “then I will send the curse upon you, and I will curse your blessings. Indeed, I have already cursed them, because you do not set it upon your heart.
verses.after: If you will not listen and will not take it to heart to honor my name,” says the LORD of Armies, “I will send the curse upon you and curse your blessings. Indeed, I have already cursed them, because you do not take it to heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: If you will not listen, and if you will not set it upon your heart to give honor to my name,” says the LORD of Hosts, “then I will send the curse upon you, and I will curse your blessings. Indeed, I have already cursed them, because you do not set it upon your heart.

verses.rationale: Follows seed as offspring, retains graphic dung and removal, and notes seed’s ambiguity.
verses.before: Look, I will rebuke your offspring, and I will spread dung upon your faces, the dung of your festival sacrifices, and you will be taken away with it.
verses.after: I will rebuke your offspring and smear dung on your faces, dung from your festivals, and you will be carried away with it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Behold, I will rebuke your offspring, and I will spread dung upon your faces, the dung of your festival sacrifices, and you shall be taken away with it.

verses.rationale: Retains the covenant’s intended continuation rather than cancellation.
verses.before: Then you will know that I have sent this command to you, that my covenant with Levi may stand,” says the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: Then you will know that I sent you this command so my covenant with Levi might continue,” says the LORD of Armies.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then you shall know that I have sent this command to you, that my covenant with Levi may stand,” says the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Keeps life, peace, and reverence distinct while easing the compressed syntax.
verses.before: “My covenant with him was one of life and peace, and I gave them to him. It was a covenant of fear, and he feared me. He stood in awe of my name.
verses.after: “My covenant with him was life and peace. I gave these to him for reverence, and he revered me; he stood in awe of my name.
verses.tsw_comparator: “My covenant with him was one of life and peace, and I gave them to him. It was a covenant of fear, and he feared me. He stood in awe of my name.

verses.rationale: Retains mouth/lips and walking images and the instruction’s effect.
verses.before: True instruction was in his mouth, and no injustice was found on his lips. He walked with me in peace and uprightness, and he turned many from iniquity.
verses.after: True instruction was in his mouth, and no injustice was found on his lips. He walked with me in peace and uprightness and turned many away from guilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: True instruction was in his mouth, and no injustice was found on his lips. He walked with me in peace and uprightness, and he turned many from iniquity.

verses.rationale: Keeps the priest as messenger and embodied speech imagery.
verses.before: For the lips of a priest should guard knowledge, and people should seek instruction from his mouth, for he is the messenger of the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: For a priest’s lips should guard knowledge, and people should seek instruction from his mouth, because he is a messenger of the LORD of Armies.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the lips of a priest should guard knowledge, and people should seek instruction from his mouth, for he is the messenger of the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Preserves three failures and the consequential misuse of instruction.
verses.before: But you have turned aside from the way. You have caused many to stumble by your instruction. You have corrupted the covenant of Levi,” says the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: But you have turned from the way. You have made many stumble through instruction. You have corrupted Levi’s covenant,” says the LORD of Armies.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you have turned aside from the way. You have caused many to stumble by your instruction. You have corrupted the covenant of Levi,” says the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Keeps the public consequence and partiality accusation.
verses.before: “So I also have made you despised and abased before all the people, inasmuch as you do not keep my ways but show partiality in your instruction.”
verses.after: “So I have made you despised and low before all the people, because you do not keep my ways and show partiality in instruction.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “So I also have made you despised and abased before all the people, inasmuch as you do not keep my ways but show partiality in your instruction.”

verses.rationale: Retains both questions and the communal us without deciding father’s identity beyond context.
verses.before: Have we not all one Father? Has not one God created us? Why then are we faithless to one another, profaning the covenant of our fathers?
verses.after: Do we not all have one father? Did not one God create us? Why do we betray one another, profaning our ancestors’ covenant?
verses.tsw_comparator: Have we not all one Father? Has not one God created us? Why then are we faithless to one another, profaning the covenant of our fathers?

verses.rationale: Retains all locations and the foreign-god daughter image rather than turning it into a racial prohibition.
verses.before: Judah has been faithless, and an abomination has been committed in Israel and in Jerusalem. For Judah has profaned the sanctuary of the LORD, which he loves, and has married the daughter of a foreign god.
verses.after: Judah has betrayed, and an abomination has been committed in Israel and Jerusalem. Judah has profaned the LORD’s holy place, which he loves, and married the daughter of a foreign god.
verses.tsw_comparator: Judah has been faithless, and an abomination has been committed in Israel and in Jerusalem. For Judah has profaned the sanctuary of the LORD, which he loves, and has married the daughter of a foreign god.

verses.rationale: Preserves the obscure paired idiom with an explicit note, without claiming a certain class distinction.
verses.before: May the LORD cut off from the tents of Jacob the man who does this, whoever he may be, even if he brings an offering to the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: May the LORD cut off from Jacob’s tents anyone who does this—one who wakes and one who answers—even one who presents an offering to the LORD of Armies.
verses.tsw_comparator: May the LORD cut off from the tents of Jacob the man who does this, whoever he may be, even if he brings an offering to the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Retains tears and rejected offerings without assigning all tears to an unstated speaker.
verses.before: And this second thing you do: You cover the altar of the LORD with tears, with weeping and groaning, because he no longer regards the offering or accepts it with favor from your hand.
verses.after: And this is another thing you do: you cover the LORD’s altar with tears, weeping, and groaning, because he no longer regards the offering or accepts it favorably from your hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: And this second thing you do: You cover the altar of the LORD with tears, with weeping and groaning, because he no longer regards the offering or accepts it with favor from your hand.

verses.rationale: Preserves the wife’s relational standing and the man’s betrayal.
verses.before: But you say, “Why does he not?” Because the LORD was witness between you and the wife of your youth, to whom you have been faithless, though she is your companion and your wife by covenant.
verses.after: You ask, “Why?” Because the LORD was witness between you and the wife of your youth, whom you have betrayed, though she is your companion and your wife by covenant.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you say, “Why does he not?” Because the LORD was witness between you and the wife of your youth, to whom you have been faithless, though she is your companion and your wife by covenant.

verses.rationale: Keeps the difficult one/spirit/offspring sequence in a qualified rendering, without pretending the syntax is settled.
verses.before: Did he not make them one, with a portion of the Spirit in their union? And what was the one God seeking? Godly offspring. So guard yourselves in your spirit, and let none be faithless to the wife of his youth.
verses.after: Did not the one make them, with a remnant of spirit belonging to him? And what was the one seeking? Offspring for God. So guard your spirit, and let no one betray the wife of his youth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Did he not make them one, with a portion of the Spirit in their union? And what was the one God seeking? Godly offspring. So guard yourselves in your spirit, and let none be faithless to the wife of his youth.

verses.rationale: Follows the third-person hates construction and preserves violence; the alternative I-hate-divorce rendering is noted without making the passage a blanket pastoral rule.
verses.before: “For I hate divorce,” says the LORD, the God of Israel, “and him who covers his garment with violence,” says the LORD of Hosts. “So guard yourselves in your spirit, and do not be faithless.”
verses.after: “For the man who hates and divorces,” says the LORD, the God of Israel, “covers his garment with violence,” says the LORD of Armies. So guard your spirit, and do not betray.
verses.tsw_comparator: “For I hate divorce,” says the LORD, the God of Israel, “and him who covers his garment with violence,” says the LORD of Hosts. “So guard yourselves in your spirit, and do not be faithless.”

verses.rationale: Retains the two complaints and their distinct claims.
verses.before: You have wearied the LORD with your words. But you say, “How have we wearied him?” By saying, “Everyone who does evil is good in the sight of the LORD, and he delights in them,” or by asking, “Where is the God of justice?”
verses.after: You have wearied the LORD with your words. Yet you ask, “How have we wearied him?” By saying, “Everyone who does evil is good in the LORD’s eyes, and he delights in them,” or, “Where is the God of justice?”
verses.tsw_comparator: You have wearied the LORD with your words. But you say, “How have we wearied him?” By saying, “Everyone who does evil is good in the sight of the LORD, and he delights in them,” or by asking, “Where is the God of justice?”

verses.rationale: Keeps messenger, Lord, covenant messenger, and repeated coming without specifying their identities.
verses.before: “Look, I am sending my messenger, and he will prepare the way before me. And the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple. And the messenger of the covenant in whom you delight, look, he is coming,” says the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: “Look, I am sending my messenger to clear a way before me. Suddenly the Lord you seek will come to his temple—the messenger of the covenant in whom you delight. Look, he is coming,” says the LORD of Armies.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Behold, I am sending my messenger, and he will prepare the way before me. And the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple. And the messenger of the covenant in whom you delight, behold, he is coming,” says the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Preserves both questions and both refining/cleaning comparisons.
verses.before: “But who can endure the day of his coming, and who can stand when he appears? For he is like a refiner's fire and like fullers' soap.
verses.after: But who can endure the day of his coming? Who can stand when he appears? For he is like a refiner’s fire and launderers’ soap.
verses.tsw_comparator: “But who can endure the day of his coming, and who can stand when he appears? For he is like a refiner's fire and like fullers' soap.

verses.rationale: Retains sitting refiner, both metals, and offerings as the result.
verses.before: He will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver, and he will purify the sons of Levi and refine them like gold and silver, and they will bring offerings in righteousness to the LORD.
verses.after: He will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver. He will purify Levi’s descendants and refine them like gold and silver, so they may present offerings to the LORD in righteousness.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver, and he will purify the sons of Levi and refine them like gold and silver, and they will bring offerings in righteousness to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps both communities and the temporal parallel.
verses.before: Then the offering of Judah and Jerusalem will be pleasing to the LORD as in the days of old and as in former years.
verses.after: Then Judah’s and Jerusalem’s offerings will please the LORD, as in days long ago, in former years.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the offering of Judah and Jerusalem will be pleasing to the LORD as in the days of old and as in former years.

verses.rationale: Preserves the entire list and makes wage exploitation explicit.
verses.before: Then I will draw near to you for judgment. I will be a swift witness against sorcerers, against adulterers, against people who swear falsely, against people who oppress the hired worker in his wages, the widow and the fatherless, against people who thrust aside the the alien and do not fear me, says the Lord of hosts.
verses.after: “I will draw near to you for judgment and be a swift witness against sorcerers, adulterers, those who swear falsely, those who cheat hired workers of wages, oppress widows and the fatherless, and turn aside the resident foreigner, and who do not fear me,” says the LORD of Armies.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I will draw near to you for judgment. I will be a swift witness against sorcerers, against adulterers, against those who swear falsely, against those who oppress the hired worker in his wages, the widow and the fatherless, against those who thrust aside the the alien and do not fear me, says the Lord of hosts.

verses.rationale: Keeps the two contrasting unchanged/not-ended statements without overexplaining their causal relation.
verses.before: “For I, the LORD, do not change. So you, O sons of Jacob, are not consumed.
verses.after: “For I, the LORD, have not changed, and you, Jacob’s descendants, have not come to an end.
verses.tsw_comparator: “For I, the LORD, do not change. Therefore you, O sons of Jacob, are not consumed.

verses.rationale: Retains the return/return reciprocity and question pattern.
verses.before: From the days of your fathers you have turned aside from my statutes and have not kept them. Return to me, and I will return to you,” says the LORD of Hosts. But you say, “How will we return?”
verses.after: Ever since your ancestors’ days you have turned away from my statutes and failed to keep them. Return to me, and I will return to you,” says the LORD of Armies. “But you ask, ‘How should we return?’
verses.tsw_comparator: From the days of your fathers you have turned aside from my statutes and have not kept them. Return to me, and I will return to you,” says the LORD of Hosts. But you say, “How shall we return?”

verses.rationale: Keeps the charge, question, and specific withheld gifts.
verses.before: “Will a man rob God? Yet you are robbing me. But you say, ‘How have we robbed you?’ In tithes and contributions.
verses.after: Will a human rob God? Yet you are robbing me. You ask, ‘How have we robbed you?’ In tithes and contributions.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Will a man rob God? Yet you are robbing me. But you say, ‘How have we robbed you?’ In tithes and contributions.

verses.rationale: Preserves the collective accusation and curse rather than individualizing it.
verses.before: You are cursed with a curse, for you are robbing me, the whole nation of you.
verses.after: You are under a curse, yet you rob me—the whole nation of you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You are cursed with a curse, for you are robbing me, the whole nation of you.

verses.rationale: Keeps storehouse food and heaven’s windows; does not turn the collective promise into a modern financial guarantee.
verses.before: Bring the full tithe into the storehouse, that there may be food in my house. And thereby put me to the test,” says the LORD of Hosts, “if I will not open for you the windows of heaven and pour out for you a blessing until there is no more need.
verses.after: Bring the whole tithe into the storehouse, so there may be food in my house. Test me in this,” says the LORD of Armies, “and see whether I will not open heaven’s windows for you and pour out blessing beyond measure.
verses.tsw_comparator: Bring the full tithe into the storehouse, that there may be food in my house. And thereby put me to the test,” says the LORD of Hosts, “if I will not open for you the windows of heaven and pour out for you a blessing until there is no more need.

verses.rationale: Preserves devourer and the vine’s fruit-loss image.
verses.before: I will rebuke the devourer for you, so that it will not destroy the fruit of your soil, and your vine in the field will not fail to bear,” says the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: I will rebuke the devourer for you, so it will not destroy the ground’s produce, and your vine in the field will not lose its fruit,” says the LORD of Armies.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will rebuke the devourer for you, so that it will not destroy the fruit of your soil, and your vine in the field shall not fail to bear,” says the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Retains the land’s delight and nations’ recognition.
verses.before: “Then all nations will call you blessed, for you will be a land of delight,” says the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: “All the nations will call you fortunate, for you will be a land of delight,” says the LORD of Armies.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Then all nations will call you blessed, for you will be a land of delight,” says the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Keeps the accusation and quoted objection.
verses.before: “Your words have been hard against me,” says the LORD. But you say, ‘How have we spoken against you?’
verses.after: “Your words against me have been harsh,” says the LORD. “Yet you ask, ‘What have we said against you?’
verses.tsw_comparator: “Your words have been hard against me,” says the LORD. But you say, ‘How have we spoken against you?’

verses.rationale: Preserves the complaint’s profit logic and mourning posture.
verses.before: You have said, ‘It is vain to serve God. What profit is there in keeping his charge or in walking as mourners before the LORD of Hosts?
verses.after: You have said, ‘Serving God is useless. What profit is there in keeping his charge or walking in mourning before the LORD of Armies?
verses.tsw_comparator: You have said, ‘It is vain to serve God. What profit is there in keeping his charge or in walking as mourners before the LORD of Hosts?

verses.rationale: Keeps the arrogant’s apparent success and testing language that echoes verse ten.
verses.before: And now we call the arrogant blessed. Evildoers not only prosper but they put God to the test and escape.’”
verses.after: Now we call the arrogant fortunate. Those who do evil prosper; they even test God and escape.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: And now we call the arrogant blessed. Evildoers not only prosper but they put God to the test and escape.’”

verses.rationale: Retains all three divine names, attentive hearing, and the remembrance book.
verses.before: Then people who feared the LORD spoke with one another. The LORD paid attention and heard them, and a book of remembrance was written before him of people who feared the LORD and esteemed his name.
verses.after: Then those who feared the LORD spoke with one another. The LORD paid attention and listened, and a book of remembrance was written before him for those who feared the LORD and honored his name.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then those who feared the LORD spoke with one another. The LORD paid attention and heard them, and a book of remembrance was written before him of those who feared the LORD and esteemed his name.

verses.rationale: Keeps treasured possession and the father/serving-son comparison.
verses.before: “They will be mine,” says the LORD of Hosts, “in the day when I make up my treasured possession, and I will spare them as a man spares his son who serves him.
verses.after: “They will be mine,” says the LORD of Armies, “my treasured possession on the day I act. I will spare them as a man spares his son who serves him.
verses.tsw_comparator: “They shall be mine,” says the LORD of Hosts, “in the day when I make up my treasured possession, and I will spare them as a man spares his son who serves him.

verses.rationale: Retains both parallel distinctions and again.
verses.before: Then once more you will see the distinction between the righteous and the wicked, between one who serves God and one who does not serve him.”
verses.after: Then you will again see the difference between the righteous and the wicked, between the one who serves God and the one who does not.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then once more you shall see the distinction between the righteous and the wicked, between one who serves God and one who does not serve him.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the oven/stubble imagery and complete root/branch loss.
verses.before: “For look, the day is coming, burning like a furnace, when all the arrogant and all evildoers will be stubble. The day that is coming will set them ablaze,” says the LORD of Hosts, “so that it will leave them neither root nor branch.
verses.after: “Look, the day is coming, blazing like an oven. All the arrogant and everyone who does evil will be stubble. The coming day will set them ablaze,” says the LORD of Armies, “leaving them neither root nor branch.
verses.tsw_comparator: “For behold, the day is coming, burning like a furnace, when all the arrogant and all evildoers will be stubble. The day that is coming shall set them ablaze,” says the LORD of Hosts, “so that it will leave them neither root nor branch.

verses.rationale: Retains sun, wings, and exuberant calf image without identifying a later referent.
verses.before: But for you who fear my name, the sun of righteousness will rise with healing in its wings. And you will go out and leap like calves from the stall.
verses.after: But for you who fear my name, the sun of righteousness will rise with healing in its wings. You will go out and leap like calves released from the stall.
verses.tsw_comparator: But for you who fear my name, the sun of righteousness shall rise with healing in its wings. And you shall go out and leap like calves from the stall.

verses.rationale: Keeps the bodily trampling and ashes image.
verses.before: You will tread down the wicked, for they will be ashes under the soles of your feet on the day when I act,” says the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: You will tread down the wicked; they will be ashes beneath the soles of your feet on the day I act,” says the LORD of Armies.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall tread down the wicked, for they shall be ashes under the soles of your feet on the day when I act,” says the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Retains servant, Horeb, all Israel, and the two instruction categories.
verses.before: “Remember the law of Moses my servant, the statutes and judgments that I commanded him at Horeb for all Israel.
verses.after: “Remember the instruction of Moses my servant, the statutes and judgments I commanded him at Horeb for all Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Remember the law of Moses my servant, the statutes and judgments that I commanded him at Horeb for all Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps named Elijah and the coming-before relation.
verses.before: Look, I am sending to you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and fearful day of the LORD.
verses.after: Look, I am sending you Elijah the prophet before the great and fearsome day of the LORD comes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Behold, I am sending to you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and fearful day of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves reciprocal family turning, specific fathers, and the technical final threat.
verses.before: And he will turn the hearts of fathers to their children and the hearts of children to their fathers, lest I come and strike the land with a decree of destruction.”
verses.after: He will turn fathers’ hearts toward their children and children’s hearts toward their fathers, so that I do not come and strike the land with a ban of destruction.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he will turn the hearts of fathers to their children and the hearts of children to their fathers, lest I come and strike the land with a decree of destruction.”
